rsguide

Diagnose remote sensing data and suggest analyses.

rsguide takes remote sensing data (satellite images, elevation models, points, polygons or tables with coordinates), automatically identifies what they are and suggests which analyses are possible. Each suggestion comes with a plain-language rationale, the necessary caveats and an example code snippet already filled in with your files and bands.

The package does not run the analyses: it diagnoses and recommends. It is aimed at ecologists and students who are new to remote sensing.

Installation 

if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("RikD96/rsguide")

System libraries on Linux

On Linux, the sf and terra dependencies are compiled from source and need system libraries (GDAL, GEOS, PROJ and others). Install them before running the commands above:

# Ubuntu
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y libgdal-dev libgeos-dev libproj-dev libudunits2-dev \
  libsqlite3-dev libtbb-dev libnetcdf-dev

# Fedora
sudo dnf install gdal-devel geos-devel proj-devel udunits2-devel \
  sqlite-devel tbb-devel netcdf-devel

On Windows and macOS, install.packages() normally downloads ready-made binaries of these dependencies, so this step is not needed.

Vignettes (optional)

The command above does not build the vignettes, which can be read online. To install them too, you need Pandoc, which comes with RStudio (from a terminal outside RStudio, it must be on your PATH), and:

install.packages(c("knitr", "rmarkdown"))
remotes::install_github("RikD96/rsguide", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Example 

library(rsguide)

# A file, an R object or a whole folder
folder <- system.file("extdata", package = "rsguide")
d <- diagnose(folder)
d                     # diagnosis and list of suggested analyses
summary(d)            # rationale and caveats of each analysis
show_code(d, "ndvi")  # code ready to copy
as.data.frame(d)      # report as a table (to save as CSV)

What diagnose() identifies:

  • type of data: raster, vector (points, lines, polygons) or table with coordinates (lon/lat, x/y, decimalLongitude/decimalLatitude…);
  • layers, resolution, coordinate reference system, extent and missing values;
  • bands and likely sensor (Sentinel-2, Landsat 4-9 or generic names such as red, nir, swir1);
  • value scale (0-1 reflectance, integers x 10,000, Landsat Collection 2, the +1000 offset of Sentinel-2…);
  • digital elevation models, class maps and time series;
  • whether vectors fall on the raster, and whether the coordinate systems match.

Analyses that can be suggested: NDVI, EVI, SAVI, NDRE, NDMI, NDWI, MNDWI, NBR, supervised and unsupervised classification, change detection, trend analysis, slope, aspect, watersheds and drainage, extraction of values at points, zonal statistics and landscape metrics.

Editable rules

Recommendations come from a table (inst/rules/rules.csv) where each row is an analysis, with the condition under which it is suggested. Inspect it with rsguide_rules() and add your own rules without touching the code:

my_rules <- rbind(rsguide_rules(), new_rule)
diagnose(folder, rules = my_rules)

Documentation

  • ?rsguide: package overview, accepted inputs and recognized sensors.
  • Case study: diagnosis of Sentinel-2 images of the Jurua River, near Cruzeiro do Sul (Acre, Brazil), from a single file to a folder with a time series, a DEM and field plots. If you built the vignettes: vignette("case-study-jurua", package = "rsguide").
  • Custom rules: how to add new analyses, write conditions and code templates. If you built the vignettes: vignette("custom-rules", package = "rsguide").
  • ?jurua_data: the example data and their sources.
